name: Plein air
summary: Work made outside in front of the subject, in the light of the place and the hour.
how: Work in front of the motif in one session of 1 to 3 hours, before the light moves.
Take the colour of shadows from the sky and the ground around them; do not paint them black.
Use the light that is there; add no lamp.

origin.note: The collapsible paint tube (John Goffe Rand, 1841) lets the Barbizon painters work outdoors in front of the motif.

adoptions.via: The Skagen painters and other Nordic painters work on the beach and in the summer night light.
Rome Open City is shot on real streets in daylight, with little added light.

sources.title: John House, Impressionism: Paint and Politics (2004)
